352	  function undo() {
353	    if (!undoStack.length) return;
354	    const previous = undoStack[undoStack.length - 1];
355	    tree = previous.tree;
356	    company = previous.company;
357	    datasetId = previous.datasetId;
358	    history = previous.history; // a true revert: the change entry goes with the change
359	    undoStack = undoStack.slice(0, -1);

364	  // Reset, import and dataset switch all replace the document, so they replace
365	  // both halves of it: a tree from one dataset beside another's org would leave
366	  // every unitId dangling.

370	    company = companyOf(datasetId);

395	  // ── export / import ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
396	  //

398	  // before it trusts anything inside. Same package on both sides, so a file

401	  let fileInput;

406	  function exportTree() {
407	    const doc = createDocument({ tree, company, history, meta: { title: getDataset(datasetId).title } });
408	    const url = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([JSON.stringify(doc, null, 2)], { type: 'application/json' }));
409	    const a = document.createElement('a');
410	    a.href = url;
411	    a.download = `okr-${new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)}.json`;
412	    a.click();
413	    URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
414	    note(`Exported ${tree.nodes.length} nodes to ${a.download}.`, { note: true });
415	  }

417	  async function importTree(e) {
418	    const file = e.target.files?.[0];
419	    e.target.value = ''; // so re-picking the same file fires change again
420	    if (!file) return;
421	
422	    const out = parseDocument(await file.text());
423	    if (!out.ok) {
424	      note(`Couldn't import ${file.name}: ${out.errors.slice(0, 3).join('; ')}`, { error: true });
425	      return;
426	    }

428	    undoStack = [...undoStack, snapshot()]; // same snapshot-then-replace as reset()
429	    tree = out.document.tree;
430	    // A file written before teams existed has no `company`; it gets an empty
431	    // org named after the file rather than keeping ours, which would claim
432	    // teams the imported tree never referenced. Its `owner` text still shows.
433	    company = structuredClone(out.document.company ?? { name: out.document.meta?.title ?? file.name, units: [] });

440	    // the boundary marker: an empty batch saying where the file came from.
441	    commit([], { actor: 'import', reason: `Imported ${file.name}`, undoable: false });

446	  // `keepEditing` is for the Detail panel's "add a child": the new node is
447	  // selected and stays in edit mode with its label focused. Every other caller

475	  function freshUnitId(name) {

  async function importTree(e) {
    const file = e.target.files?.[0];
    e.target.value = ''; // so re-picking the same file fires change again
    if (!file) return;

    const out = parseDocument(await file.text());
    if (!out.ok) {
      note(`Couldn't import ${file.name}: ${out.errors.slice(0, 3).join('; ')}`, { error: true });
      return;
    }

    undoStack = [...undoStack, snapshot()]; // same snapshot-then-replace as reset()
    tree = out.document.tree;
    // A file written before teams existed has no `company`; it gets an empty
    // org named after the file rather than keeping ours, which would claim
    // teams the imported tree never referenced. Its `owner` text still shows.
    company = structuredClone(out.document.company ?? { name: out.document.meta?.title ?? file.name, units: [] });
    history = structuredClone(out.document.history ?? emptyHistory());
    resetSession();
    // The snapshot above already covers the import, so this commit only writes
    // the boundary marker: an empty batch saying where the file came from.
    commit([], { actor: 'import', reason: `Imported ${file.name}`, undoable: false });
    const warned = out.warnings.length ? ` ${out.warnings.length} warning${out.warnings.length === 1 ? '' : 's'}: ${out.warnings.slice(0, 3).join('; ')}` : '';
    note(`Imported ${tree.nodes.length} nodes from ${file.name}. Undo to go back.${warned}`, { note: true });
  }

  let settleTimer;
  let framePending = false;
  let frameMs = 900;

old = """  // A document the graph has not laid out yet has no positions worth framing:
  // graphData() re-heats the simulation, and the nodes are still stacked at the
  // origin for the first few hundred ms. Mount and every document swap wait the
  // same beat, so the overview always arrives the same way.
  export function frameWhenSettled(delay = 700, ms = 900) {
    clearTimeout(settleTimer);
    settleTimer = setTimeout(() => frameAll(ms), delay);
  }
"""
new = """  // A document the graph has not laid out yet has no positions worth framing:
  // graphData() re-heats the simulation, and a tree of any size goes on growing
  // for a second or more — a frame taken too early crops a tree that had not
  // finished expanding. So frame twice: once on a short delay, so a swap never
  // leaves the user staring through the old camera, and once when the engine
  // actually stops, which is the frame that is right. On a small tree the
  // engine wins the race and there is only the one move.
  const SETTLE_HINT = 700;

  export function frameWhenSettled(ms = 900) {
    clearTimeout(settleTimer);
    frameMs = ms;
    framePending = true;
    settleTimer = setTimeout(() => frameAll(ms), SETTLE_HINT);
  }

  // Armed only by frameWhenSettled, so the engine stopping after an ordinary
  // edit — every graphData() re-heats it — does not yank the camera.
  function onSettled() {
    if (!framePending) return;
    framePending = false;
    clearTimeout(settleTimer);
    frameAll(frameMs);
  }

  // `f` shortcut and every document swap share it, so the move always looks the
  // same. It goes through flyTo rather than the library's zoomToFit: zoomToFit

  export function frameAll(ms = 900) {

  // graphData() re-heats the simulation, and a tree of any size goes on growing
  // for a second or more — a frame taken too early crops a tree that had not
  // finished expanding. So frame twice: once on a short delay, so a swap never
  // leaves the user staring through the old camera, and once when the engine
  // actually stops, which is the frame that is right. On a small tree the
  // engine wins the race and there is only the one move.
  const SETTLE_HINT = 700;

  export function frameWhenSettled(ms = 900) {

    frameMs = ms;
    framePending = true;

  }

  // Armed only by frameWhenSettled, so the engine stopping after an ordinary
  // edit — every graphData() re-heats it — does not yank the camera.
  function onSettled() {

  const SETTLE_STEP = 150;  // how often to look

The settle poll fires too eagerly during slow phases of the expansion. Let me have the camera track the expansion instead of guessing when it ends:

Assistant2026-09-12T17:40:41.029Z
$ Bash
Track the expansion rather than guessing the settle
python3 - <<'PY'
p='web/src/Graph.svelte'
s=open(p).read()
old = """  // A document the graph has not laid out yet has no positions worth framing:
  // graphData() re-heats the simulation and the tree goes on expanding for a
  // second or so, and a frame taken mid-expansion crops the result. The
  // engine's own stop signal is no use here — force-graph runs a fixed 15 s
  // cooldown and only then reports a stop — so watch the thing we actually
  // care about and frame once the tree has stopped growing.
  const SETTLE_STEP = 150;  // how often to look
  const SETTLE_MAX = 4000;  // never leave the camera behind longer than this

  export function frameWhenSettled(ms = 900) {
    clearTimeout(settleTimer);
    const deadline = performance.now() + SETTLE_MAX;
    let last = -1;
    const look = () => {
      const r = spread();
      // Grown by under a percent since the last look, or out of patience.
      if ((r > 0 && r <= last * 1.01) || performance.now() > deadline) {
        frameAll(ms);
        return;
      }
      last = r;
      settleTimer = setTimeout(look, SETTLE_STEP);
    };
    settleTimer = setTimeout(look, SETTLE_STEP);
  }
"""
new = """  // A document the graph has not laid out yet has no positions worth framing:
  // graphData() re-heats the simulation and the tree goes on expanding for a
  // second or more, so a single frame is either too early (and crops) or too
  // late (and the user stares through the old camera meanwhile). The engine's
  // own stop signal is no help — force-graph runs a fixed 15 s cooldown and
  // only then reports a stop.
  //
  // So don't guess when the growing ends: follow it. Re-frame every step until
  // the tree stops growing. Each frame only slides the camera along its current
  // bearing, and each retargets a tween already in flight, so the repeats read
  // as one continuous pull-back rather than a series of jumps.
  const SETTLE_STEP = 150;  // how often to look
  const SETTLE_MAX = 5000;  // stop following eventually, however lively the layout

  export function frameWhenSettled(ms = 900) {
    clearTimeout(settleTimer);
    const deadline = performance.now() + SETTLE_MAX;
    let last = -1;
    const follow = () => {
      const r = spread();
      frameAll(ms);
      // Half a percent of growth since the last look is done growing.
      if ((r > 0 && r <= last * 1.005) || performance.now() > deadline) return;
      last = r;
      settleTimer = setTimeout(follow, SETTLE_STEP);
    };
    settleTimer = setTimeout(follow, SETTLE_STEP);
  }
"""
assert s.count(old)==1
s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)

Tool reply2026-09-12T17:45:56.129Z
  function frame(nodes, aim, ms) {
    levelCamera(ms);
    let r = 0;
    for (const n of nodes) {
      r = Math.max(r, Math.hypot(n.x - aim.x, n.y - aim.y, n.z - aim.z) + nodeRadius(n));
    }
    const dist = Math.max(MIN_DIST, fitDistance(r * FRAME_MARGIN));
    // Approach along the camera's current bearing so the move feels continuous.
    const cam = graph.cameraPosition();
    const dir = new THREE.Vector3(cam.x - aim.x, cam.y - aim.y, cam.z - aim.z);
    if (dir.length() < 1) dir.set(0, 0.3, 1);
    dir.normalize();
    // Azimuth is preserved, so the move still reads as "from where I was".
    if (Math.abs(dir.y) > MAX_Y) {
      const h = new THREE.Vector3(dir.x, 0, dir.z);
      if (h.lengthSq() < 1e-6) h.set(0, 0, 1);
      h.normalize().multiplyScalar(Math.sqrt(1 - MAX_Y ** 2));
      dir.set(h.x, Math.sign(dir.y) * MAX_Y, h.z);
    }
    const to = { x: aim.x + dir.x * dist, y: aim.y + dir.y * dist, z: aim.z + dir.z * dist };
    // A NaN here does not just lose one move: the next frame reads the camera
    // back to work out its bearing, so one bad write poisons every move after
    // it and the view never recovers. Drop it instead.
    if (!Number.isFinite(to.x) || !Number.isFinite(to.y) || !Number.isFinite(to.z)) return;
    (window.__probe ??= []).push([Math.round(performance.now()), nodes.length, Math.round(r), Math.round(dist), Math.round(Math.hypot(cam.x-aim.x,cam.y-aim.y,cam.z-aim.z))]);
    graph.cameraPosition(to, aim, ms);
  }

  // An arbitrary set of nodes with no single subject: aim at their centroid.
  // A node counts as positioned only when all three coordinates are: one NaN
  // among them poisons the centroid, and through it the camera.

  const MAX_Y = Math.cos((20 * Math.PI) / 180);

  // The one framing move: pull back along the current bearing until everything
  // in `nodes` fits, aiming at `aim` rather than at the world origin (which is
  // all `zoomToFit` can do).
  function frame(nodes, aim, ms) {
    levelCamera(ms);
    let r = 0;
    for (const n of nodes) {
      r = Math.max(r, Math.hypot(n.x - aim.x, n.y - aim.y, n.z - aim.z) + nodeRadius(n));
    }
    const dist = Math.max(MIN_DIST, fitDistance(r * FRAME_MARGIN));
    // Approach along the camera's current bearing so the move feels continuous.
    const cam = graph.cameraPosition();
    const dir = new THREE.Vector3(cam.x - aim.x, cam.y - aim.y, cam.z - aim.z);
    if (dir.length() < 1) dir.set(0, 0.3, 1);
    dir.normalize();
    // Azimuth is preserved, so the move still reads as "from where I was".
    if (Math.abs(dir.y) > MAX_Y) {
      const h = new THREE.Vector3(dir.x, 0, dir.z);
      if (h.lengthSq() < 1e-6) h.set(0, 0, 1);
      h.normalize().multiplyScalar(Math.sqrt(1 - MAX_Y ** 2));
      dir.set(h.x, Math.sign(dir.y) * MAX_Y, h.z);
    }
    const to = { x: aim.x + dir.x * dist, y: aim.y + dir.y * dist, z: aim.z + dir.z * dist };
    // A stage with no size yet — the first frames after mount, or a collapsed
    // pane — gives the camera a 0/0 aspect, and fitDistance hands back NaN. The
    // cost of writing that through is not one lost move: the next frame reads
    // the camera back to work out its bearing, so one NaN poisons every move
    // after it and the view never recovers. Skip the move instead; the caller
    // that is following a settling layout will come round again.
    if (!Number.isFinite(to.x) || !Number.isFinite(to.y) || !Number.isFinite(to.z)) return;
    graph.cameraPosition(to, aim, ms);
  }

  // An arbitrary set of nodes with no single subject: aim at their centroid.
  // A node counts as positioned only when all three coordinates are: one NaN
  // among them poisons the centroid, and through it the camera.
  const placed = (n) => Number.isFinite(n.x) && Number.isFinite(n.y) && Number.isFinite(n.z);

  export function flyTo(ids, ms = 1200) {
    if (!graph || !ids?.length) return;
    clearTimeout(hoverTimer);
    hovered = null;
    const want = new Set(ids);
    const nodes = graph.graphData().nodes.filter((n) => want.has(n.id) && placed(n));
    if (!nodes.length) return;
    const c = { x: 0, y: 0, z: 0 };
    for (const n of nodes) { c.x += n.x; c.y += n.y; c.z += n.z; }
    c.x /= nodes.length; c.y /= nodes.length; c.z /= nodes.length;
    frame(nodes, c, ms);
  }

  // Selecting a node frames its neighbourhood but keeps the node itself centred:
  // the selection is what the panel is about, so it is what the eye holds.
  export function focusNode(id, ms = 800) {
    if (!graph || !id) return;
    clearTimeout(hoverTimer);
    hovered = null;
    const want = new Set(neighborhoodOf(tree, id));
    const nodes = graph.graphData().nodes.filter((n) => want.has(n.id) && placed(n));
    const self = nodes.find((n) => n.id === id);
    if (!self) return; // no position yet: leave the camera where it is
    frame(nodes, { x: self.x, y: self.y, z: self.z }, ms);
  }

  // Frames the whole tree and levels the horizon. The mount-time overview, the
  // `f` shortcut and every document swap share it, so the move always looks the
  // same. It aims the same measure-and-solve flyTo uses at every node rather
  // than calling the library's zoomToFit, which estimates the distance from
  // where the nodes happen to land on screen right now: from a camera sitting
  // inside the tree that estimate is meaningless, and a swap that arrived
  // zoomed in stayed zoomed in.
  export function frameAll(ms = 900) {
    if (!graph) return;
    flyTo(graph.graphData().nodes.map((n) => n.id), ms);
  }

  // A document the graph has not laid out yet has no positions worth framing:
  // graphData() re-heats the simulation and the tree goes on expanding for a
  // second or more, so a single frame is either too early (and crops the tree)
  // or too late (and the user stares through the old camera meanwhile). The
  // engine's own stop signal is no help — force-graph runs a fixed 15 s
  // cooldown and only then reports a stop.
  //
  // So don't try to find the moment the growing ends: follow it. Re-frame every
  // step for as long as a layout plausibly takes to settle. Each frame only
  // slides the camera along its current bearing, and each retargets a tween
  // already in flight, so the repeats read as one continuous pull-back rather
  // than a series of jumps — and the last one lands on the finished tree.
  const SETTLE_STEP = 150;    // how often to re-frame
  const SETTLE_WINDOW = 2500; // how long to keep following

  export function frameWhenSettled(ms = 900) {
    clearTimeout(settleTimer);
    const until = performance.now() + SETTLE_WINDOW;
    const follow = () => {
      frameAll(ms);
      if (performance.now() < until) settleTimer = setTimeout(follow, SETTLE_STEP);
    };
    settleTimer = setTimeout(follow, SETTLE_STEP);

  // apart, and a wall-clock window would expire after one or two looks with the
  // tree still half-grown. Counting steps costs a slower follow there and lands
  // on the same frame.
  const SETTLE_STEP = 150;  // ms between looks
  const SETTLE_STEPS = 16;  // ~2.4 s of following in a tab that is being watched

  export function frameWhenSettled(ms = 900) {
    clearTimeout(settleTimer);
    let left = SETTLE_STEPS;
    const follow = () => {
      frameAll(ms);
      if (--left > 0) settleTimer = setTimeout(follow, SETTLE_STEP);
    };
    settleTimer = setTimeout(follow, SETTLE_STEP);
  }

python3 - <<'PY'
p='web/src/Graph.svelte'
s=open(p).read()

old = """  // Pending settle-then-frame (see frameWhenSettled).
  let settleTimer;
"""
new = """  // An in-progress settle-then-frame (see frameWhenSettled): how many more
  // looks it owes, when the next one is due, and the flight time to use.
  let settleLeft = 0;
  let settleNext = 0;
  let settleMs = 900;
"""
assert s.count(old)==1
s=s.replace(old,new)

old = """  // Counted, not timed: a backgrounded tab has its timers throttled to seconds
  // apart, and a wall-clock window would expire after one or two looks with the
  // tree still half-grown. Counting steps costs a slower follow there and lands
  // on the same frame.
  const SETTLE_STEP = 150;  // ms between looks
  const SETTLE_STEPS = 16;  // ~2.4 s of following in a tab that is being watched

  export function frameWhenSettled(ms = 900) {
    clearTimeout(settleTimer);
    let left = SETTLE_STEPS;
    const follow = () => {
      frameAll(ms);
      if (--left > 0) settleTimer = setTimeout(follow, SETTLE_STEP);
    };
    settleTimer = setTimeout(follow, SETTLE_STEP);
  }
"""
new = """  // The follow is counted in looks and driven from the render loop rather than
  // from a timer, because the render loop is the clock the layout itself runs
  // on: force-graph ticks the simulation once per rendered frame. A tab nobody
  // is looking at renders nothing, so it lays out nothing — and a wall-clock
  // timer there would burn all its looks on a tree that had not moved since the
  // last one. On the render loop the follow simply pauses with the layout and
  // picks up where it left off.
  const SETTLE_STEP = 150;  // ms between looks
  const SETTLE_STEPS = 16;  // ~2.4 s of following

  export function frameWhenSettled(ms = 900) {
    settleMs = ms;
    settleLeft = SETTLE_STEPS;
    settleNext = performance.now() + SETTLE_STEP;
  }
"""
assert s.count(old)==1
s=s.replace(old,new)

# drive it from animate()
old = """  function animate() {
    if (upTween) {"""
new = """  function animate() {
    if (settleLeft > 0 && performance.now() >= settleNext) {
      settleLeft--;
      settleNext = performance.now() + SETTLE_STEP;
      frameAll(settleMs);
    }
    if (upTween) {"""
assert s.count(old)==1
s=s.replace(old,new)

old = """    frameWhenSettled();
    animate();

    return () => {
      cancelAnimationFrame(raf);
      clearTimeout(hoverTimer);
      clearTimeout(settleTimer);
"""
new = """    frameWhenSettled();
    animate();

    return () => {
      cancelAnimationFrame(raf);
      clearTimeout(hoverTimer);
"""
assert s.count(old)==1
s=s.replace(old,new)
assert 'settleTimer' not in s
open(p,'w').write(s)
print("ok")

  // timer there would burn all its looks on a tree that had not moved since the

Assistant2026-09-12T17:55:11.588Z

Done. Loading a document is now treated as a reset across all three entry points.

App.svelte — one resetSession() that the dataset picker, Import, and Reset all call: clears highlight/preview/selection/edit mode, closes the panel, replaces the chat tabs with a single fresh one, and re-frames the 3D view. It replaces four lines that were duplicated in each of the three paths. undo() also re-frames, but only when it swaps the dataset back — otherwise the camera would stay framed on a node of the tree that just left.

Chat.svelte — the suggestion chips used to require a literally empty tab, so the "Loaded …" note would have suppressed them. They now show until someone actually takes a turn; notes and errors don't count. The block moved below the messages so it follows any note.

Graph.svelte — frameWhenSettled(). Two real bugs surfaced here:

  • frameAll used the library's zoomToFit, which estimates distance from where nodes land on screen. From a camera sitting inside the graph that estimate is meaningless — switching to the 135-node dataset while zoomed in left the camera at distance 94 when 1100 was needed. It now uses the same measure-and-solve flyTo already used for node focus.
  • A single frame after the swap is always wrong: graphData() re-heats the simulation and the tree keeps expanding. The engine's own stop signal is useless (force-graph runs a fixed 15s cooldown). So the camera now follows the expansion for 16 looks, counted off the render loop rather than a timer — the render loop is the clock the layout itself ticks on.

Also hardened frame(): a zero-size stage gives the camera a 0/0 aspect and fitDistance returns NaN; writing that through didn't just lose one move, it poisoned every subsequent one, since each frame reads the camera back for its bearing.

Verified in the browser: switching datasets from a deep zoom frames the whole tree exactly (measured 1099 against a computed 1096 for the 135-node set; 565/565 and 548/548 for the others), the chat collapses to one tab with chips restored, an open interview tab is closed, the assistant's highlight clears, and undo re-frames back. 16/16 tests pass.

One judgment call worth flagging: I included the Reset button in this, since it reloads the dataset from scratch and the name promises it — say the word if you'd rather Reset kept the conversation.

Done — resetSession() now empties the undo stack, which pulled three other things with it:

  • The snapshots those paths pushed are gone. Reset, switch, and import each did undoStack = [...undoStack, snapshot()] right before replacing the document; clearing the stack a few lines later made those dead weight.
  • The notes no longer offer an undo. "Loaded … Undo to go back." and "Imported … Undo to go back." would have pointed at a button that's now disabled. They're plain statements of what landed.
  • The re-frame branch I added to undo() last round is removed. It fired when an undo entry's datasetId differed from the current one — only possible via those three snapshots. Every remaining entry comes from commit() on the document already on the stage, so the branch was unreachable.

Verified in the browser: added a team (Undo (1)) → switched datasets → Undo greyed with no count, Teams count replaced by the new document's own, note reads "Loaded "Regional clinic network, FY26" (30 nodes)." with chips restored. Same for the Reset button. And ordinary undo still works — added a team, clicked Undo, teams went 24 → 23 with "Reverted the last change." 16/16 tests pass.
